facts.about: Incorporated in 2010, Eternal Limited (previously Zomato Limited) is one of the leading online Food Service platforms in terms of the value of food sold. Its offerings include food delivery, dining-out services, Loyalty programs, and others. As of December 31, 2020, Eternal has established a strong footprint across 23 countries with 131,233 active food delivery restaurants, 161,637 active delivery partners, and an average monthly food order of 10.7 million customers.

flags.text: Operating margin expanded 19 pts in 3 years (-17% → 2.2%)
Operating cash flow was negative over 5 years (₹49 cr) despite ₹-949 cr of profit
Latest quarter growth (+78%) well below 3-yr trend (+97%)

business.summary: Eternal Ltd. is a technology platform services provider operating in food delivery, quick commerce, B2B supplies, and going-out segments. It generates revenue through commissions and direct sales of goods via its inventory-led model.

segments.name: India food ordering and delivery
segments.note: Revenue grew 26% YoY driven by higher order volumes and per-order revenue.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.note: Revenue grew 626% YoY due to shift to an inventory-led model.

segments.name: Going-out
segments.note: Revenue grew 32% YoY across dining-out, movies, and events categories.

segments.name: B2B supplies
segments.note: Revenue declined 13% YoY due to scaling down non-restaurant business.

guidance.statement: Over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish.
guidance.quote: It's hard to project or comment on margin trajectory every quarter but broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish.

guidance.statement: We maintain that guidance as of now.
guidance.quote: It's very early on that three-year journey; we're still two quarters in, so I don't want to jump too much into the future. We maintain that guidance as of now.

guidance.statement: We expect NOV growth to pick up starting the December quarter on a YoY basis.
guidance.quote: That's right. ... We're talking about NOV growth pickup starting the December quarter on a YoY basis?

guidance.statement: We think at this point we're likely to end at the higher end of the range.
guidance.quote: We think at this point we're likely to end at the higher end of the range that we had guided earlier and hence, the communication.

guidance.statement: We are targeting a GAAP EBIT margin of 4% as long-term.
guidance.quote: And then you get to a GAAP EBIT margin of 4% as long-term?

guidance.statement: We expect capex per store to be lower than INR 2.5 crore going forward.
guidance.quote: If you therefore look at our capex over the last six months, nine months or a longer period, and the capex per store for that period, you will find it is lower than INR 2.5 crore. We expect that to continue going forward.

guidance.statement: We remain firmly on track for our guidance of 3,000 stores by March.
guidance.quote: On store addition, we're on track on our guidance for March of 3,000 stores. We remain firmly on track.

guidance.statement: We have given overall guidance of 60% CAGR for quick commerce.
guidance.quote: We've given overall guidance of 60% CAGR and that would obviously mean some reasonable store expansion, but we're not planning to give out any specific number guidance on that.

guidance.statement: We will get to 5-6% margin at some point in quick commerce.
guidance.quote: As we move to 5-6% margin that we are saying we will get to at some point, contribution margin will go up and on a year-on-year basis, we'll see that trend consistently.

guidance.statement: We have extremely high confidence in the business model to deliver 5% to 6% of NOV margins.
guidance.quote: In the long term, in our letter we have mentioned that our confidence on margins going to 5% to 6% of NOV remains high

guidance.statement: We now expect the losses to come down sequentially from here towards breakeven in the next four to six quarters.
guidance.quote: Irrespective of that, as we have mentioned in question 13, we now expect the losses to come down sequentially from here towards breakeven in the next four to six quarters.

guidance.statement: We expect year-on-year growth to continue slowly trending up towards 20% YoY.
guidance.quote: As of now, as we have mentioned, we expect year-on-year growth to continue slowly trending up towards 20% YoY, is what our current sense on the market is.

guidance.statement: We expect to deliver 30% CAGR over the next three to four years.
guidance.quote: For us to deliver 30% CAGR over the next three to four years, it doesn't necessarily mean that the industry has to grow that much.

scorecard.promised: Expect margins to remain flattish over the next 1 or 2 years.
scorecard.delivered: Margins rose slightly from 2.9% in Jun 2026 to 3.1% in Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Margin moved from 2.9% to 3.1% QoQ, remaining within a tight range as guided.

scorecard.promised: Overall guidance of 60% CAGR for quick commerce over the next 3 years.
scorecard.delivered: Revenue grew 77.6% YoY in Sep 2026, down from 182% in Jun 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Current growth of 77.6% remains well above the 60% CAGR target despite the sharp deceleration.

scorecard.promised: Expect losses to come down sequentially towards breakeven in 4-6 quarters.
scorecard.delivered: Company reported a PAT of ₹125 cr in Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: PAT has remained positive for nine consecutive quarters, reaching ₹125 cr in the latest period.

scorecard.promised: Expect year-on-year growth to continue slowly trending up towards 20% YoY.
scorecard.delivered: Revenue growth was 77.6% YoY in Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Growth is significantly higher than the 20% floor suggested in Q3 FY26.

scorecard.promised: Confidence in delivering 5% to 6% of NOV margins in the long term.
scorecard.delivered: Current margin stands at 3.1% as of Sep 2026.
scorecard.evidence: With margins at 3.1%, a 1.9-2.9 percentage point expansion is still required for the long-term goal.

narrative.scoreline: Management has successfully transitioned to profitability and exceeded growth floors, though recent sharp deceleration in revenue growth warrants caution.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Management wants to maintain margins broadly while reinvesting in growth.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Margins have stayed between 2.8% and 3.1% over the last three quarters.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Inventory losses are asymptotic and not expected to get materially better.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Operating margins have stagnated around 2.2% to 3.1% annually.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Capex per store will be lower than INR 2.5 crore going forward.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: FCF was negative ₹1,114 cr in FY26 despite positive PAT, suggesting high investment.

bull: Revenue grew 77.6% YoY in Sep 2026, significantly outperforming the long-term 60% CAGR guidance.
Company has maintained positive PAT for nine quarters, reaching ₹125 cr in the latest period.
Operating margins expanded 19 points over three years, moving from -17% to 2.2% in FY26.
bear: Revenue growth decelerated sharply from 182% in Jun 2026 to 77.6% in Sep 2026.
Free Cash Flow remains deeply negative at -₹1,114 cr for FY26 despite reported accounting profits.
100% of loans and advances were given to related parties, raising significant governance concerns.
watch: Check if Sep 2026 revenue growth deceleration to 77.6% stabilizes or continues downward.

claims.claim: We want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth to drive the growth upwards.
claims.quote: Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards.

claims.claim: The bulk of new store expansion will be in smaller cities, where paybacks are extremely good.
claims.quote: Directionally, we've also mentioned in the letter that the bulk of the expansion of these new stores will be in smaller cities. We do expect that to be the focus from here on.

claims.claim: It is a nascent zero-to-one bet that could generate high shareholder value if it works.
claims.quote: If it works, it's a global business and it will generate extremely high shareholder value over the next few years. But if it doesn't work, it's something we'll kill.

claims.claim: Competition is more predictable now, providing an opportunity to become more aggressive on infrastructure expansion.
claims.quote: But now, as we mentioned last time also, competition is more predictable now, and that provides an opportunity for us to become more aggressive on infrastructure expansion.

claims.claim: Discount-led growth is not sustainable in the business and we expect this to not continue.
claims.quote: We strongly feel that discount-led growth is not sustainable in the business. That is what has become predictable and so we are able to more confidently plan our next few quarters.

claims.claim: We do not expect NAOV to grow from here and expect it to remain in the same range.
claims.quote: Generally, Aditya, we're not expecting the NAOV to grow from here. If you look at year-on-year, it's flat. That accounts for seasonality for Q1, and we broadly expect NAOVs to remain in the same range.

claims.claim: Inventory losses are at 1.8% of NOV and we do not expect it to be materially better.
claims.quote: It has been fairly asymptotic so far. We don't expect it to be materially much better.

claims.claim: We are seeing extremely low cost of customer acquisition, so we continue to keep marketing spends high.
claims.quote: We feel a lot of our competitors in the market have pulled back on this so we're seeing extremely low cost of customer acquisition and we, therefore, continue to see value in keeping marketing spends high at this point.

claims.claim: Our growth is driven by assortment expansion, geographical expansion, and demand densification.
claims.quote: It's a function of assortment expansion, geographical expansion as well as more demand densification in the cities where we are present today and we might also get into newer cities.

claims.claim: We optimize for absolute profit rather than profit margin percentage.
claims.quote: the objective is to optimize for growth of absolute profit and not the profit margin percentage.

claims.claim: Margin expansion is a multi-variable problem with no linear correlation to competitive intensity alone.
claims.quote: It’s a multi-variable problem with no linear correlation with just one variable.

claims.claim: Lower throughput is a function of assortment expansion, which is a long-term strategy.
claims.quote: As I mentioned, a lot of our store additions, not just last quarter but last two, three quarters, has been towards assortment expansion and as we now further expand assortment, the turnover of this long tail is not as high

claims.claim: Capex per store will increase due to investments in automation and warehousing infrastructure.
claims.quote: Even though we might see capex per store going up over the next few quarters, we don't expect net working capital to be beyond those 18 days that we had shared earlier

risks.text: Company faces uncertainty regarding GST orders received from authorities in respect of delivery charges.
Climate change risks pose threats to business operations, impacting last-mile deliveries and customer dining.
100% of loans and advances were given to related parties as of March 31, 2026.
